# `srs context`

```text
Addressability context-query commands (ext:addressability)

Usage: srs context [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  field   Assemble context for a single field: current value, aiGuidance
  record  Assemble context for a record: field values, inbound and outbound relations with neighbours inline; with the global --container <ID>, also its arrangement subtree there
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --repo <REPO>
          Repository path (defaults to auto-detect from current directory)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - json: JSON output (default)
          - yaml: YAML output
          - text: Human-readable text output (planned, currently returns diagnostic)
          
          [default: json]

      --store <STORE>
          Storage backend override. By default the backend is inferred from the repository location
          
          [possible values: file, json]

      --pretty
          Pretty-print JSON output (no effect on text format)

      --container <CONTAINER_ID>
          Container scope: constrains list/create/delete to this container's membership; on `context record` it adds the record's arrangement subtree in this container

      --actor <ACTOR>
          Session actor for everything this invocation creates (RFC-046 `createdBy`): JSON `{"kind":"human|ai","id":"<non-empty>","name":"<optional>"}`. Defaults to the `SRS_ACTOR` environment variable; with neither, creations are unattributed. Host configuration only — a request payload never carries it. An invalid value refuses every creating command (`actor-invalid`); a corpus below dataModelRevision 9 refuses an actor session (`revision-too-old`) until `repo apply-migration --id rfc046-actor-provenance`. A `.srsj` migrated in memory on open refuses every write first (`migration-required-before-write`) until its migrations are applied

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `srs context record`

```text
Assemble context for a record: field values, inbound and outbound relations with neighbours inline; with the global --container <ID>, also its arrangement subtree there

Usage: srs context record [OPTIONS] <RECORD_ID>

Arguments:
  <RECORD_ID>
          Record instance ID

Options:
      --exclude-category <CATEGORY>
          Omit edges whose relation type has this category (repeatable), e.g. `--exclude-category composition --exclude-category sequence` drops structural edges

      --repo <REPO>
          Repository path (defaults to auto-detect from current directory)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - json: JSON output (default)
          - yaml: YAML output
          - text: Human-readable text output (planned, currently returns diagnostic)
          
          [default: json]

      --projection <PROJECTION>
          How much of each neighbour to inline: `full` (whole record, default), `card` (id, label, type, lifecycle state, one summary line) or `label` (id and label)
          
          [default: full]

      --markdown
          Return the context as compact markdown in `rendered` (card projection unless `--projection label`): one line per edge with label, type and instance id

      --store <STORE>
          Storage backend override. By default the backend is inferred from the repository location
          
          [possible values: file, json]

      --pretty
          Pretty-print JSON output (no effect on text format)

      --container <CONTAINER_ID>
          Container scope: constrains list/create/delete to this container's membership; on `context record` it adds the record's arrangement subtree in this container

      --actor <ACTOR>
          Session actor for everything this invocation creates (RFC-046 `createdBy`): JSON `{"kind":"human|ai","id":"<non-empty>","name":"<optional>"}`. Defaults to the `SRS_ACTOR` environment variable; with neither, creations are unattributed. Host configuration only — a request payload never carries it. An invalid value refuses every creating command (`actor-invalid`); a corpus below dataModelRevision 9 refuses an actor session (`revision-too-old`) until `repo apply-migration --id rfc046-actor-provenance`. A `.srsj` migrated in memory on open refuses every write first (`migration-required-before-write`) until its migrations are applied

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```
